newsitem.title: USA: Tommy Hilfiger says net jumps 56 percent; stock climbs.
newsitem.headline: Tommy Hilfiger says net jumps 56 percent; stock climbs.

text.p: Tommy Hilfiger Corp., the men's and boys' sportswear retailer, said Monday its earnings jumped 56 percent in the latest quarter and announced plans to open its first international flagship store in Britain.

The company said its earnings increased to $27.4 million, or 72 cents a share, in its fiscal third quarter ended Dec. 31, from $17.6 million, or 47 cents a share, a year earlier. Revenues were also strong, rising to $188.2 million from $130.5 million.

"Contributing to our sales increase was the continued success of our products across the board," said Joel Horowitz, chief executive officer. "As a result of a strong Christmas selling season, we saw a solid increase in our retail business and continued healthy gains in our men's and boys' wholesale businesses."
The retailer said its first international flagship store in London is expected to open in 1998.
Tommy Hilfiger's stock was up $1.50 to $52.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
